phase: 15.5 — DEFLATE decompression ablation over the real real100-v1 members
measured_commit_subject: phase15.5: SIMD-safe endstream scan, miniz SIMD adler, DEFLATE-ablation court
tree_state: the measured binaries are built from src at e676166 (clean); the only dirty entries were edits to tools/phase15-deflate-court.sh made while fixing the court itself, which do not affect the measured code
corpus: real100-v1 — the REAL compressed members of the frozen corpus: PDF FlateDecode zlib streams + ZIP method-8 DEFLATE members extracted from 88 documents with extractable members (52,498 members, 481 MiB compressed, 2,768 MiB decoded)

miniz_simd_adler.verdict: correct, below the 1.25x bar; free and output-preserving, so it is enabled in the shipped build

zlib_rs.verdict: MEETS the pre-registered bar (>=1.25x, <=1.10x RSS) and is byte-identical to the reference

zune_inflate.verdict: DISQUALIFIED — decoded 255 members differently from the reference; speed is irrelevant when the bytes differ

correction_gate: the reference is miniz_oxide; any candidate whose output differs is disqualified regardless of speed
interpretation: zlib-rs is a real, correct decompression win over the shipped miniz_oxide (1.58x GB/s, RSS-neutral) and meets the pre-registered adoption bar. zune-inflate is faster but wrong on 255 members — a valuable negative. miniz_oxide's SIMD adler path is a free, correctness-preserving 1.11x and is enabled.
recommended_next_change: swap the shipped inflate backend to zlib-rs behind the existing inflate boundary, guarded by this byte-identity witness; not done in this court (the court measures only)
part_a: the scalar PDF `find_endstream` substring scan was replaced with a reused memchr::memmem::Finder (differential tests assert equality with the retained scalar oracle); it is not separately timed here — the end-to-end effect is material only for large/scanned PDFs
caveats: 88 of 100 documents contributed members; 12,001 members were declined (unsupported filters) and are counted, not hidden

miniz SIMD vs scalar was initially inconclusive because `cargo build` does not build examples and a shared target dir handed back the scalar example for the simd feature set; the sealed run builds each arm explicitly (--example, separate target dir) and the simd arm reports config=simd
no `perf` in the lane; the harness reports its own peak RSS and /usr/bin/time -v agrees
tuning: none; the corpus members and the candidate set are pre-registered; the adoption bar was fixed before measuring
